subject: homeschool.subject_ang
hint: Some plurals don't add -s: man → men, child → children. -f → -ves: wolf → wolves.
intro: Most nouns add -s: one cat, two cats. Some nouns change: one man → two men, one child → two children, one mouse → two mice. Words ending in -f or -fe often take -ves: one wolf → two wolves, one knife → two knives. A few stay the same: one sheep → two sheep.

subject: homeschool.subject_ang
hint: 's = belongs to: Sam's dog = the dog of Sam.
intro: To show that something belongs to someone, add 's to the owner: the bike of Emma → Emma's bike. The owner comes first, then the thing: the bone of the dog → the dog's bone. Don't forget the apostrophe: Emmas bike ✗, Emma's bike ✓.

subject: homeschool.subject_ang
hint: -e → add -d. Consonant + y → -ied. Short word ending in vowel + consonant → double it.
intro: Most verbs add -ed: jump → jumped. Verbs ending in -e just add -d: like → liked. Consonant + y → -ied: cry → cried, but vowel + y → -yed: play → played. Short verbs ending in one vowel + one consonant double the consonant: stop → stopped.

subject: homeschool.subject_ang
hint: Irregular verbs don't take -ed: go → went, not goed.
intro: Some verbs have their own past form. You have to learn them: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, fly → flew. Never add -ed to them: Yesterday I went to the park ✓, Yesterday I goed ✗.

subject: homeschool.subject_ang
hint: Capital at the start, for names and for the word I. End with a period, or a question mark for a question.
intro: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a period (.) or a question mark (?) for a question. Names of people, places, days and months always take a capital: Emma, Canada, Monday, May. The word I is always a capital: Noah and I play.

subject: homeschool.subject_ang
hint: Two ideas = two sentences. Cut where the second idea starts.
intro: When two ideas are glued together, cut them into two sentences. I like dragons they can fly ✗ → I like dragons. They can fly. ✓ A comma is not enough between two full ideas: I like dragons, they can fly ✗.
